items.title: Joe Bushkin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: my group with Buck Clayton, Milt Hinton and Jo Jones

ctx.x: And you played mostly for dancing at these ballrooms?

Yeah it was back in the 30’s, the early 30’s, and into the swing era. And I played intermission piano at Kelly’s Stables when the Coleman Hawkins Quartet was there, and I was at the Embers. I could go on endlessly, where — we opened the Embers in New York which became the hot jazz venue and we were there for nine weeks and believe it or not I was there with Milt Hinton, Buck Clayton, Jo Jones on drums, that was the quartet, and Art Tatum was there appearing.
Did you guys play one set?

items.title: 67246_Buck Clayton oral history interview
items.q: I also during those years when I was working with Joe Bushkin, I had my own band and he was one of the members of the band.

ctx.x:
Yes, I had to play soft in there because it was a small, well they would ask you to play softly. I don't care who it was, they eventually, Ralph Watkins did never put it in my contract to play soft, but I would automatically play soft because that's the kind of music that would be affiliated with Joe Bushkin, mute, but not everything.
I could play open without playing loud. But he has had it in the contract, keep your mute in at all times. Other trumpet players, that's been in their contract. But it was never in…
Yes, yes. That's really what they want.
